paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I'll say so once. God told Ezekiel that the desire of his eyes was about to be taken, and then He told him not to weep (Ezekiel 24:16). Ezekiel did as he was commanded the next morning (Ezekiel 24:18). I think that was the hardest obedience in the whole book, and I don't have a joke for it.

Here's why it matters. Ezekiel's loss was a sign, and the people asked what it meant for them (Ezekiel 24:19). God answered that He was about to desecrate His sanctuary, the pride of their power and the desire of their eyes (Ezekiel 24:21). They had leaned on that place like it could never fall, and God was telling them to look at Him instead. Everything they trusted in could be taken, but the One who spoke to them stays, and the whole point was that they would know He is the Lord GOD (Ezekiel 24:24).

So here's what I'm carrying out of the oven, baker. When something you love is taken, or something you trusted turns out to be shaky, God hasn't gone silent on you. In this passage He keeps speaking, and Ezekiel's mouth is promised to open again when the news comes (Ezekiel 24:27). It's a hard word, and it points to the God who is worth trusting more than anything else we lean on. The ovens stay ready, friend, and the story isn't over.
